GMI-T0.constraint: Universal-computation non-result: fully owned by P0.UNIVERSALITY + P0.INVARIANCE_THESIS; state T0 as 'D0 and the execution/description components of D1 are theorems of the parents and carry no intelligence-specific content'; cite Dershowitz Thm 5 (unique maximal effective model) and the invariance thesis.

Cite AIXItl (Hutter 2007 Thm 14, cost O(2^l t), author's own 'typing monkeys' remark) and universal ABO (R&S Def 15, §6.3 concatenation on a k-times faster machine) as the canonical universal-computation-only constructions: any Track-B basis whose predictive content reduces to these is a non-result. T0 should state that an enumerative or concatenative optimum over all programs carries zero information about which sub-family wins.

Finn & Levine Lemma 4.1 is the learning-law instance of the universal-computation non-result: any permutation-invariant learning procedure is representable by representation + one gradient step; T0 should cite it and state that identifying content must come from bounded compilation or ecology-relative efficiency, never from representability.

Strengthen the non-result: universality of *stochastic* programs (Church; ACR sec. 1.1 'the class of computable distributions') is also non-evidence; a random tape adds no intelligence-specific content.

P7.POLY_DYNAMICAL_SYSTEMS supplies the universal-computation non-result for automata ('every dynamical system can be obtained by wiring together memoryless ones'; all machines embed into synchronous machines); Learn (Fong et al.) is likewise a universal-computation-sized category of update rules. GMI-T1.constraint: Finite basis closure: trivial via Shepherdson-Sturgis (P/Q/J suffice); T1 is non-trivial only if 'adaptive generating basis' adds an update/verify primitive whose closure is NOT the partial recursive functions - i.e. T1 must be a closure statement about update rules, not about computed functions.
Not constrained by this family (no finite-basis results); note only that L_M is finite by physical size in R&S (e.g. 2^{2^26} programs), which trivialises closure.

VSML's V_M (~2,400 shared parameters with sparsity) and Sandler's genome (k x k matrices + 4 scalars) are existing finite bases whose closure over learning laws is demonstrated only by examples; T1 must state closure conditions these bases lack.

Any finite-basis closure claim for the probabilistic morphology must use a *partial* conditioning primitive: Church's query (positive-measure predicates), Staton's norm (fails on evidence 0/∞), or Gen's generate/update weights — because a total computable conditioning operator does not exist (ACR).

Fong et al. Example V.3 (five primitive learners generate all quadratic-error backprop nets under the SMC grammar) and Krohn-Rhodes (simple groups + flip-flop are the forced primes of finite automata) are existing finite-basis closure results for two morphologies; T1 must cite both and add only cross-morphology basis closure.

GMI-T10.constraint: Finite morphology phase boundary: constrained by NFL-over-P(f)'s (advantage sums to a constant across the simplex of ecologies, so the phase diagram is conservative) and by Blum (regions where no fastest morphology exists must be admitted); the boundary, if any, is predicted by this family to lie along the verification-contract axis (Levin/Hutter exact-verifier regime vs. statistical regime).

Competes with R&S §7 conjecture that ABO designs are stable over wide variations in machine speed/size and environment complexity; T10 must specify the regime (too-small or too-powerful M, or price/horizon changes) where finitely many boundaries appear. Hay Ex 4 (context inversion, non-indexability) and R&S Thms 4-6 (optimal sequence structure changes with deadline distribution) are the family's only phase-like dependencies.

GPICL Fig. 2, 4, 7, 10 supply the empirical template: control parameters = number of tasks, model size, state size N_S, task batch size; phases = plateau / memorize / task-identify / generalize; bimodal solution clusters at the boundary. T10 must produce a prospective boundary (candidate: Baxter's n-bound in C(eps, H^n_l) vs. state size), which no parent has.

ACR's computability boundary in observation structure is a genuine hard phase boundary that is not continuously approachable (σ→0 non-uniformity, sec. 9.3); T10 should ask whether this boundary coincides with the morphology boundary between trace-measure and point-estimate systems.

No parent; the closest structural handle is the semiring parameter in Dudzik-Velickovic (real vs tropical) and the CRDC choice (Smooth vs POLY_Z2) — natural candidate axes for a finite phase boundary.

GMI-T11.constraint: Morphology recovery identifiability: constrained by Rice (semantic labels undecidable) and enabled by Hoyrup/Brossard (decidable for c.e.-total or (T,N)-bounded classes via anticomplexity/enumeration); T11 must define recovery as a decidable intensional predicate on a bounded class.

Constrained negatively: Leike-Hutter Cor 9 and Thm 11 imply morphology cannot be identified from finite behaviour alone (any finite behaviour is optimal under some prior; lookup tables are dense in Upsilon); recovery must use internal structure or resource signatures on a fixed reference machine.

Recovery/identifiability tools that exist: VSML introspection (Fig. 9), Sandler symmetry test, Wang's model-fitting of learned behavior to Rescorla-Wagner with varying learning rate, Duan's regret comparison; all behavioral or negative. T11 needs a structural identification of the emergent law.

Identifiability of the probabilistic morphology from behaviour is underdetermined (Prop 8.3 / Thm 26 / Venture 2.7: many programs, one posterior); recovery must use resource signatures (scaling with data, particles, KL) — the only invariants the quotient does not erase.
Krohn-Rhodes gives partial identifiability for automata (simple-group divisors are invariants of any cascade); nothing analogous exists for the other morphologies in this family.

GMI-T12.constraint: Developmental morphogenesis: Solomonoff/AIXI own acquisition in the limit; Levin search gives the cost law time = O(2^{K(mu)}) (conceptual jump size, Ozkural eq. 12 citing Solomonoff/Schmidhuber); Blum says the developmental revision chain need not converge; T12 is non-parent only if it predicts WHICH morphology the resource-bounded developmental process passes through, which no parent does.

Open in every parent: Hutter 2007 §7.2 (training not addressed), R&S §7 (learning component and self-rewriting open; learning external in §5), Chollet (curricula are inputs, developer-aware GD charges the initial state). T12 must supply what none supplies; Chollet's developer-aware GD is the right scoring rule for it.

Developmental morphogenesis of learning laws is owned for the neural substrate under gradient/ES outer loops (VSML, GPICL, Wang, RL^2, Sandler, learned optimizers); T12's residual is cross-paradigm morphogenesis and prospective prediction.

The PLoT's 'effective language changes with learning', BPL's learning-to-learn over a fixed DSL, and Venture 11.2's speculative inference optimizers are the family's only D2/D12 material; none shows acquisition of the conditioning machinery itself — T12 must treat query/norm as either innate to the basis or show its emergence.
No parent addresses developmental acquisition; every construction is designer-instantiated. T12 is entirely residual.

GMI-T2.constraint: Basis equivalence / bounded compiler relation: the execution component IS the first-machine-class equivalence (poly time, const space); T2 is either (a) a sub-polynomial refinement (model-dependent by the thesis itself) or (b) the extension to update/verify/revise components; Accattoli-Dal Lago warn that establishing a reasonable cost model for a morphology (e.g. counting rewrite steps or forward passes) can be a research problem in itself (size explosion).

Leike-Hutter Table 1 (compiler sizes K_U(U'), K_U'(U)) with Thm 6/Cor 9 show constant-overhead compilers between reference machines can reverse optimality within lifetime m; T2's bounded-compiler relation must therefore be stated relative to horizon/lifetime and must include verification work (AIXItl needs proofs of VA(p) with length l_P and setup O(l_P^2 2^{l_P})).

Bounded compilers between learning-law bases exist: Sandler Eq. 4 (backprop -> genome, zero overhead), VSML learning-algorithm cloning (backprop -> shared LSTM substrate, O(W N^2), lossy 87-90% vs SGD), Andrychowicz App. D (BFGS -> NTM-BFGS, asserted). Use the Gen GFI and van de Meent's FOPPL⇓graphical-model / HOPPL→messaging-interface compiles as the reference bounded compilers; the only explicit overhead statements in the family are Venture's linear-vs-quadratic regeneration and enumeration's exponential-in-#choices vs rejection's exponential-in-KL — T2 should adopt these as compile-overhead exemplars.

Basis equivalence / bounded compiler relations exist as algebra maps between machine presentations (SSV Prop 5.1.1 DDS -> Mch^td; Niu-Spivak lens ≅ coalgebra ≅ retrofunctor) and as the equivalence Alg_Endo(F) ≅ Alg_Mnd(F^kappa) (CDL Thm B.16); T2 must charge the PSPACE-hard/NP-complete costs these parents note but do not model.

GMI-T3.constraint: Morphology equivalence quotient: the quotient by polynomial simulation collapses all sequential morphologies to one class and all unboundedly-parallel ones to a second; a morphology-discriminating quotient must be finer (resource-vector or sub-polynomial) and, to be decidable, intensional/resource-bounded (Rice, Hoyrup).

Both Upsilon and Feasible(M) quotient programs to agent functions; R&S use program identity. T3 must define the intermediate quotient; the family shows the two extremes are useless for morphology (too coarse: identical Upsilon; too fine: every program its own class).

Sandler Section 3.5 symmetry test (d Delta w_ij / d w_mn = d Delta w_mn / d w_ij) is a concrete invariant separating gradient-flow laws from non-gradient laws; T3's quotient over learning laws can start from it, adding Finn & Levine's kernel form and metric-gradient-flow classes.

Morphology-equivalence quotient for the probabilistic class = equality of (score,result) measures (Staton Prop 8.3), kernels as quotient of random functions (Heunen Thm 26), Venture 2.7 declarative readings; T3 must *refuse* this quotient as-is and enrich it with charged cost, since the quotient discards scaling behaviour.

Morphology equivalence quotient = reparametrisation 2-cells in Para (Cruttwell Def 2.3; CDL Def G.1) and Fong et al.'s equivalence of learners; weight tying is a quotient by a comonoid (CDL Thm G.10).

GMI-T5.constraint: Gradient/backprop update derivation: constrained by Blum (no optimal update program in general) and by Levin/Hutter (any update rule is discoverable by universal search at 2^{l(p)} cost, so 'derivation' must beat that constant to be non-trivial).
Not constrained (no gradient/update derivation; learning in R&S §5 is external agnostic PAC; AIXI 'learns' by eliminating inconsistent Turing machines, Hutter 2009 §5g).
Owned by VSML cloning and Sandler Eq. 4: backprop/SGD is derivable inside both a recurrent message-passing basis and a multi-state genome basis; T5 must not re-derive, only cite and generalize.

Gradient/backprop update appears in the family only as (a) the reparameterized ELBO gradient (VAE) and (b) the E_{p(y)}KL proposal gradient (Le) — both with conditioning as the *target*; T5 should state gradient update as the point-estimate degeneration of conditioning and price the degeneration.

PARENT_SUFFICIENT: gradient/backprop update = Para(R) for a CRDC plus optimiser reparametrisation (Cruttwell et al.), functor L_{eps,e} (Fong et al.), AD as homomorphism (Elliott), reverse chain rule RD.5 (Cockett et al.).

GMI-T6.constraint: Probabilistic-program/Bayes specialization: owned by P0.SOLOMONOFF + P0.MDL_OCCAM - Bayes = Solomonoff restricted to a computable class with prior 2^{-K}; MDL variants = MAP/Jeffreys/prequential specializations; T6 must add the resource-bounded selection (which class, at what budget) to be non-parent.

Largely owned: AIzeta = Bayes mixture over a class M (Hutter 2007 §4.2), universal Bayes (Hutter 2011 eqs 3-7), MC-AIXI Def 4/Prop 1/Thm 3 give the probabilistic-program/Bayes specialization with self-optimising guarantees for stationary ergodic n-Markov classes; T6 should absorb 'class restriction + prior' as the derivation and claim only what is left (the choice law).

Not owned by this family. Meta-RL compares against Gittins/Thompson/PSRL (Bayes-optimal) baselines and GPICL cites Bayesian-inference interpretations of in-context learning (Ortega 2019; Mikulik 2020; Mueller 2022): T6 must absorb those missing parents before claiming a Bayes specialization.

State Bayes specialization as: coherent real-valued Boolean belief ⇒ conditional probability (Terenin-Draper Thm 16; de Finetti/Mundici Thm 2.7), computable exactly iff observation is computably discrete with positive mass (ACR Prop 9.2), or admits a positive bounded computable conditional density (Prop 9.4, Cor 9.6), or is corrupted by independent noise with bounded computable density (Cor 9.7), or is exchangeable with computable de Finetti measure (sec. 9.4); noncomputable and non-uniformly approximable otherwise (Thm 7.6, Cor 8.5, Thm 6.7, sec. 9.3). This is the P5-class limit for T6.

Bayes specialisation is owned at the type level: exact inversion is a section of the Stat-fibration (Smithe Thm 5.2 / Cor 5.3) and approximate inference is a lax section with loss (statistical games, free energy); T6 should be re-cut as 'resource-selected loss model', not as a new bridge.

GMI-T7.constraint: Production/rewrite specialization: Levin/Hutter search natively produces programmatic/symbolic morphologies under exact verifiers; T7 should state under which verification contract rewrite systems are the Levin-optimal output.

Partially constrained: R&S §4.2 'fixed sequence of decision procedures' with bounded-optimal ordering (Lemmas 3-5, Thm 3 DP, Thms 4-6 closed forms) is a production-like morphology whose optimal structure depends on the deadline distribution; T7 can use it as the minimal production-system phase example, but rules are black boxes.
No parent in this family produces production/rewrite learning laws; untouched.
Minor: the compilation relation ⇓ (van de Meent) and Church's unfold/PCFG idioms show rewrite systems are absorbed as generative programs; T7 gains no new mechanism here.
OPEN in this family: no parent gives an optic/lens learning law for production/rewrite systems; Wilson-Zanasi covers circuits, not rewriting; Krohn-Rhodes covers automata structure, not learning.

GMI-T8.constraint: Programmatic specialization: same as T7; Hutter Thm 2 (fastest is among the shortest provably-equivalent programs) is the parent result linking program length and speed for this family.

Partially constrained: AIXItl/Levin search/OOPS and Chollet's ARC-as-program-synthesis speculation; no theorem selects programmatic morphology. Speed Prior gives Kt as the programmatic simplicity measure.
No parent produces programmatic learning laws (AutoML-Zero and Li & Malik's policy view are cited but the emergent objects are neural/optimizer policies); untouched here, presumably P3.

Program induction is conditioning over program space (Church sec. 5, BPL, PLoT sec. 7, Venture 2.9.3 inverse interpretation); T8 must separate 'programmatic' from 'probabilistic' by resource profile (point-estimate search vs trace-measure conditioning), not by law.

Partial: Elliott (programs reinterpreted as differentiable maps) and Dudzik-Velickovic (DP as semiring integral transform) give the forward bridge; no parent gives a programmatic learning law (search/enumeration) as an optic — T8's learning half is open.

GMI-T9.constraint: Ecology relativity / no universal morphology: fully owned by P0.NFL (W&M, SVW, Igel-Toussaint, Wolpert 2020 over P(f)'s); T9 adds nothing unless it names the non-c.u.p. property of intelligence ecologies and derives a positive dominance from it.

Strongly supported at policy level: Leike-Hutter (UTM relativity, trivial Pareto), R&S (bounded optimality defined relative to (M,𝓔)), Veness Limitations (PST class fails outside its ecology), Chollet (scope-relative). T9 must lift this to morphology level and must not restate the policy-level result.

Ecology relativity of learning laws is already evidenced: Wang Fig. 2f (structured-prior training hurts on independent arms), Duan Table 2 (advantage reverses with episodes), Finn & Levine Sec. 7 (gradient vs recurrent meta-learners diverge OOD), Wichrowska/VeLO failure boundaries, Baxter's (P, Q) environment; T9 should cite these as the no-universal-learning-law instances.

Ecology relativity is supported empirically: Anglican Fig. 2 (line permutation flips PMCMC vs RDB dominance), Marsaglia case, Le Fig. 4 crossover, Omniglot Table 1 augmentation crossover — no parent proves it; T9 can cite these as existence proofs of non-dominance within the probabilistic class.

No parent constrains T9; but the family's ecology-blindness is itself evidence for T9's premise: the same algebra admits every base category/monad/optimiser, so dominance must come from outside the algebra (resources/ecology).
